column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: Elemental structures require a metallic/high-pressure route; ionic counting is not diagnostic.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.

column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.

column81: max_sites applies separately to empty-space maxima and metal-motif centers.
column82: Sites are geometry-derived candidate empty-space centers, not predicted ELF maxima. Distances minus covalent radii are a size convention, not electron-accessible volume. Critical cage ratios are literature heuristics for regular same-element s-orbital cages; mixed/irregular cages and orbital occupation require separate reasoning. Metal-motif centers use triangles/tetrahedra among each metal's nearest 12 metal neighbors, including distance ties; centers are ranked by nearest-nucleus distance divided by the source motif's largest radius, not by an electride likelihood. Site detection and connectivity are resolution dependent.
column86: Periodic rank 0/1/2/3 means isolated pocket/channel/sheet/network in the geometric mask. Boundary crossing alone is not percolation. This is not electronic dimensionality.

column26: Density and volume describe packing, not pressure or stability. Symmetry is tolerance dependent.
column37: A positive sum is formal electron availability under the stated oxidation assignment, not a measured interstitial occupation. Zero/negative sums do not exclude electrides. Mixed valence, polyatomic anions, covalent bonding, and metal reduction can change this accounting.
column64: Covalent-radius contacts are geometric hypotheses, not bond orders. N2/O2 group charges are alternatives, not length-derived assignments.
